findings.title: Inquiry returns to the unresolved event
findings.claim: The command to return the envoy and ask about the women's affair reopens a weighty prior event as a public, knowledge-producing inquiry.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries return through ٱرْجِعْ, an envoy through الرَّسُولُ, and formal questioning through سْـَٔلْ. The exact 12:51 context supplies the weighty matter, solicitation, testimony, and knowledge that give those focus forms a concrete public destination; the inquiry therefore turns an interrupted release into an examination of the earlier event.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the return as a change in where the unresolved matter lives: it moves from a private accusation toward named testimony and a question whose answer can become known.
findings.containment: The plain sequence remains intact: the king summons Joseph, the envoy reaches him, Joseph sends the envoy back, and asks about the women and their scheme. The finding adds the public reopening supplied by 12:51 and does not claim that the focus alone resolves the event or that the nominated context branch is the lexical meaning of every focus word.

epistemic.reason: The channel evidence is trusted, its focus and 12:51 carriers are exact, and every nominated branch has an independent trigger and focus return.

findings.title: Information before movement
findings.claim: The focus's return command extends an earlier ordering in which truthful information is delivered and checked before the person or benefit whose arrival is pending.
findings.mechanism: The prison context places a report and Lord-taught knowledge before the next arrival, while the focus places investigation before Joseph's own arrival. The focus's return also carries a verbal response back to the authority source, and 12:46 supplies a later knowledge-through-return parallel.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the delay as an ordering of events: the case must travel through knowledge and verification before bodily release or institutional movement occurs.
findings.containment: The royal command and Joseph's tactical delay remain the plain events. The information-first policy is a qualified contextual inference from the supplied sequence; a tactical delay without a general policy remains live, and unresolved HFT branch records receive no invented gloss.

epistemic.reason: Exact Arabic context and focus carriers are supplied, but HFT segmentation and unresolved branch identities are attributed nominations and target morphology is absent.

findings.title: Layered jurisdiction
findings.claim: The focus's your lord and my Lord pairing can hold a differentiated jurisdiction: public human judgment handles the inquiry while divine lordship remains the encompassing source of knowledge and authority.
findings.mechanism: The prison discourse supplies a contrast between divided lords and one compelling authority, alongside warrant and judgment language. Those context carriers meet the two focus forms of ربّ, so the alternating possessive references become a procedural distinction rather than an unqualified equivalence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the focus addresses the envoy's human authority and then closes with Joseph's divine witness: the case can be investigated publicly without making public jurisdiction the whole horizon.
findings.containment: The focus still directs the envoy to his lord and identifies Joseph's Lord as knowing the scheme. The jurisdictional allocation is a qualified contextual inference; it does not deny ordinary alternation between master and God or turn the human king into a merely symbolic figure.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is exact in its supplied context coordinates, but its unresolved branch identities and role descriptions remain attributed, with no target morphology supplied.

findings.title: The scheme remains real while moral scope widens
findings.claim: The focus names a real scheme for inquiry, while the following sequence narrows scheme into betrayal under hidden conditions and places even the vindicated self under moral scrutiny.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries the women's deliberate scheme through كَيْدِهِنَّ. The context then supplies betrayal, absence, the failed guidance of betrayers' schemes, a refusal of complete self-exoneration, and the inward النفس; the repeated scheme carrier meets these independent contacts without erasing the original accusation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the concrete charge and the later moral caution together: the case is investigated as real evidence, yet agency is not assigned to an entire category or removed from the self.
findings.containment: The focus still says that Joseph's Lord knows their scheme and still directs an inquiry about the women. The later moral widening is qualified by uncertainty about voice continuity in 12:52-53 and does not declare Joseph guilty, innocent in every respect, or the women morally uniform.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and 12:52-12:53 carriers are supplied by the HFT trace, but several branch records are unresolved and the scope-widening relation remains attributed contextual inference.

findings.title: The second summons changes the terms of arrival
findings.claim: The later repetition of the king's summons shows the focus's refusal functioning as a transformation gate: the first arrival seeks an object to be brought, while the second receives a speaking, trusted, and empowered interlocutor.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries the king, the bring command, and the return that interrupts it. At 12:54 the royal subject and bring command recur, then direct speech is followed by public standing, empowerment, and trust; the repeated form therefore meets a materially changed aftermath.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see that Joseph's postponement changes the quality of access itself: arrival after inquiry is no longer merely transport into court.

findings.title: Knowledge becomes a qualification for custody
findings.claim: The focus's divine knowledge of a hidden scheme later meets Joseph's own knowledge and guardianship, so knowledge can become a qualification for preserving vulnerable resources.
findings.mechanism: The focus closes with عَلِيمٌ, while 12:55 joins storehouses, guardianship, and knowledge in Joseph's self-description. The repeated knowledge carrier meets the new custody domain, shifting the epistemic vocabulary from defensive disclosure toward accountable administration.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the inquiry as testing truth-sensitive agency that later matters in governance, not only as a defense against a past accusation.
findings.containment: The focus still names divine knowledge of the women's scheme, and 12:55 can also mean technical competence. The custody ethic is a qualified contextual extension, not a claim that the focus explicitly predicts Joseph's appointment or that knowledge alone establishes fitness.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and 12:55 carriers are supplied, but the HFT trace is legacy-unbound and the move from knowing to custody is an attributed contextual inference.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the question as an active procedure: it does not merely request a report but creates conditions in which hidden testimony may be expressed and differentiated.
findings.containment: This remains a process analogy, not the lexical meaning of asking and not a claim that the focus describes agricultural pressing. The exact 12:49 connection also carries counter-evidence that the royal summons adds no agricultural meaning; the pressure image is retained only as a bounded local way of seeing the inquiry.

epistemic.reason: The exact carriers and focus returns are supplied, but the outlier is explicitly exploratory, one branch is unresolved, and the target morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: An external authority horizon
findings.claim: The explicitly added Fātiḥa titles widen the focus's exchange between human and divine authority into a bounded horizon of divine lordship and judgment without replacing the local inquiry.
findings.mechanism: The external occurrence رَبِّ in 1:2 returns through the focus's رَبِّكَ and رَبِّي, while مَٰلِكِ in 1:4 returns through the focus's concrete ٱلْمَلِكُ. These direct root contacts add the external descriptions of all-world lordship and judgment-day sovereignty to the focus's local human procedure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the focus's human investigation as locally real and yet held within a wider divine horizon that the added recitation context makes newly audible.
findings.containment: This is an external overlay only: 12:50 does not itself mention worlds or judgment day, the human king is not turned into a divine ruler, and the Fātiḥa material does not rank against or erase the native pericope readings. The other added ayat do not supply a further local focus contact that changes this finding.

epistemic.reason: The exact external context supplies word-level root contacts, but no support record, target morphology, or candidate nomination accompanies this overlay; its changed-reading claim is therefore exploratory and bounded.
